clue.text: Fellow falling behind laying the patio?

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
lagging means trailing or falling behind the rest

explanation.surface: A slow workman is behind schedule while paving the patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling behind' looks like the definition, since flagging can mean tiring; the definition is the question at the end, where a patio is paved with flagstones, or flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Paving a patio with flat stones is called flagging, the stones being flags or flagstones.

clue.text: Alfred coming up to follow sporting event

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Alf is the usual short form of the name Alfred
to trace someone is to follow their trail

explanation.surface: A man called Alfred arrives to watch a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Alfred is shortened to its familiar form, which 'coming up' turns into FLA, as a down clue reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race run with no jumps or hurdles is a flat race, a common racing fixture.

clue.text: An economy by diocese having a severe effect

parts.note: a cut is a saving or economy, as in spending cuts
Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Church budget cuts in a diocese are hitting people hard.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England, and a favourite crossword diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Something felt acutely is felt intensely, so the word describes a sharp, severe impact.

clue.text: Frivolous characters imprisoned by rigid dynast

indicators.note: the letters wanted are held captive within the run of the words rigid dynast

explanation.surface: A stern ruling dynasty locks up light-hearted people.
explanation.definitionFit: A giddy person is flighty and silly, lacking seriousness.

clue.text: No actual opportunity, when going round US city, to show indifference

parts.note: non is French for no, and serves as a negative prefix

indicators.note: the word for opportunity encircles the city abbreviation

parts.note: a real opportunity is a chance
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a missed chance to tour an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: NON is French for no; 'when' is only a link, and 'going round' wraps the opportunity word round the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonchalance is a calm, casual unconcern, the same as indifference.

clue.text: It's black in far from fresh beastly place

indicators.note: the letter for black goes inside the word for not fresh

parts.note: stale food is far from fresh
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dark, musty animal shed smells far from fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable is where horses and other beasts are housed.

clue.text: Paper has to move fast describing holiday property

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper
to hare is to run very quickly

explanation.surface: A newspaper rushes out a feature on a holiday home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' looks as though it signals a container, but here it only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeshare is a jointly owned holiday flat or villa, each owner using it for set weeks of the year.

clue.text: The result of excessive lying?

parts.note: reads as the outcome of telling untruths, but means a sore from lying in bed too long

explanation.surface: A habitual liar faces the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests dishonesty; the clue means lying down for a long time, which gives a pressure ulcer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressure ulcer forms on bedridden patients who lie in one position too long.

clue.text: College runner on terrace

parts.note: a runner is a river in crosswords; the Exe flows through Devon
Ter. is the abbreviation for Terrace in street addresses

explanation.surface: A college athlete trains on a terraced bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in Devon, England; Exeter is a college of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter College is one of the colleges that make up Oxford University.

clue.text: Come up against new tribe in the interior, in profusion

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the word for border on

parts.note: to abut is to border on or meet
Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: Explorers meet many tribes deep in the interior.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan, one of the twelve tribes of Israel, is a crossword favourite; 'in the interior' wraps the come-up-against word round both short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something present in profusion is plentiful, the sense of abundant.

clue.text: Has mud, for instance, brought about dirty mark?

parts.note: has can be shortened to 's, as in he's done

indicators.note: to bring a ship about is to turn it round, so the abbreviation is turned back

explanation.surface: Getting covered in mud, say, leaves a dirty stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a smear or blot of dirt.

clue.text: Piping brings ruminants back by start of year

indicators.note: the word for the animals is read backwards

parts.note: deer are cud-chewing animals

indicators.note: only the first letter of year is used

explanation.surface: A shepherd's pipe calls the animals home at the year's start.
explanation.definitionFit: A piping voice is thin and high, which is what a reedy voice sounds like.

clue.text: Greets character showing precipitation

parts.note: to hail someone is to greet them
tone can mean the character or quality of something

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting reveals someone's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumps of ice falling from the sky are a form of precipitation.

clue.text: Popular foreigner, clever, not to be removed

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an alien is a foreign national
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: A well-liked, bright immigrant cannot be deported.
explanation.definitionFit: An inalienable right cannot be taken away or transferred.

clue.text: Where you could see Victorians making an exhibition of themselves

definitions.text: Where you could see Victorians making an exhibition of themselves

parts.words: Where you could see Victorians making an exhibition of themselves
parts.note: reads as people showing off, but refers to the glass building of the Great Exhibition of 1851

explanation.surface: Prim Victorians are caught behaving badly in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Exhibition was held in London's Hyde Park in a vast glass and iron hall; 'making an exhibition of themselves' means staging the show, not misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1851 Great Exhibition, where Victorian Britain displayed its industry, was housed in this glass hall.

clue.text: Islander maintains a suspect has abandoned island

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An island resident insists that a suspect has fled the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has abandoned' takes I (island) out of MAINTAINSA; 'suspect' rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tasmanian is a native of Tasmania, the island state of Australia.

clue.text: Rascal is upsetting woman

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is distressing a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarissa is a woman's name, as in Richardson's novel.

clue.text: Not dispatched by one with mind to be hard-headed?

parts.note: something not dispatched is unsent
I is the Roman numeral one
mental means of or with the mind

explanation.surface: A letter left unposted by a thoughtful person shows a practical outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-headed person is practical and unswayed by feelings or sentiment.

clue.text: Find a French safety device

parts.note: un is the French for a
an earth wire is an electrical safety connection

explanation.surface: Someone finds a French electrical safety gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the safety wire in a plug is called the earth (US ground).
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or discover it.

clue.text: Country where large quantity of wine is reverse of first-class

parts.note: a tun is a large cask, a measure of wine

indicators.note: the term for first-class is written backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, read here as the letters AI

explanation.surface: In one nation a huge vat of wine is anything but top quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse of' turns AI (A1, first-class) into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African nation on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Plan that is put by man to mother

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for that is to say
he refers to a man
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A man explains his plan to his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet) is a less familiar abbreviation for 'that is', used in older texts beside the commoner i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or diagrammatic plan.

clue.text: Rather more splendid person applying sanction

definitions.meaning: comparative of fine, meaning more excellent
one who imposes a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: A grander figure hands out penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a comparative meaning more excellent, and someone who imposes a monetary penalty.

clue.text: Film for storing chief changes

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the five letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss alters the archive film.
explanation.definitionFit: Microfiche is a flat sheet of film on which documents are stored in miniature.

clue.text: Listener with head covering for little nipper?

parts.note: the ear is what listens
a wig covers the head

explanation.surface: A small child listens out for a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little nipper' suggests a small child; it is an insect with pincers that nip.
explanation.definitionFit: This small insect has pincers at its tail and can nip.

clue.text: You can count on them putting copper in one HQ square

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the chemical symbol is placed inside the word for headquarters
the chemical symbol is placed inside the word for headquarters

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer is posted to a single headquarters square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer; it is the metal, by its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Frames of beads on wires are counting devices, so you can literally count on them.

clue.text: Longing to have feature in silver

indicators.note: the facial feature sits inside the silver symbol

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Wanting a silver ornament on one's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Aching for something means yearning for it.

clue.text: Made rare sort of sugar

indicators.note: sort as a verb means to arrange, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rare kind of sugar has been produced.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a brown cane sugar named after a region of Guyana.
